events.description: An engineer starts setting up multiple PostgreSQL servers in staging to try out pgpool-II for load balancing queries (infrastructure#259).

Prior to starting the work, the engineer takes an LVM snapshot of the production database and loads it into the staging environment, a more up-to-date copy than the automatic daily one (which runs at 01:00 UTC).

GitLab.com experiences an increase in database load, suspected to be spam; many users cannot post comments on issues and merge requests. Getting load under control takes several hours. Part of the load came from a background job trying to remove a GitLab employee's data after their account was accidentally scheduled for removal.

Due to increased load, PostgreSQL secondary replication lags and fails because WAL segments were already removed from the primary; WAL archiving was not in use, so the secondary must be manually re-synchronised.

Engineers wipe the secondary's data directory and run pg_basebackup, which hangs silently; it reports it cannot connect because max_wal_senders is insufficient. max_wal_senders is raised from 3 to 32, but PostgreSQL fails to restart due to too many semaphores (max_connections had been set to 8000), so it is reduced to 2000 and PostgreSQL restarts successfully. pg_basebackup still hangs; strace shows it stuck in a poll call.

An engineer suspects pg_basebackup left files in the secondary's data directory from earlier attempts; it is later revealed that pg_basebackup silently waits for the primary to start sending data, which was not documented in runbooks or official docs.

While trying to restore replication, an engineer wipes the PostgreSQL data directory on the primary instead of the secondary. The process is terminated a second or two later, but around 300 GB of data has already been removed.
Engineers search for database backups and ask for help on Slack; the process of finding and using backups fails completely.

The pg_dump backups are found to be missing: the S3 bucket is empty because the backup procedure used pg_dump 9.2 against PostgreSQL 9.6, causing errors and termination. Cronjob error notifications were rejected by the receiver because DMARC was not enabled for those emails, so the failures went unnoticed.
The GitLab.com database is restored without webhooks.
Final restoration procedures are completed, including restoring webhooks, and operations are confirmed to be normal.
